items.t: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang; tech stocks surge
items.d: Nvidia's board brought Huang back as CEO with immediate effect, under two weeks after ousting him, citing US government assurances. Nvidia shares jumped over 30%, leading a sharp rebound after last week's AI sell-off.

items.t: Ukrainian drones hit Russian warship in Libya, Zelensky says
items.d: Zelensky said Ukraine struck a Russian navy ship at a Libyan port, far from the front line. The Kremlin warned of rising regional tensions but did not directly confirm the attack.

items.t: Mexican soldiers attacked after drug lord's arrest
items.d: Gunmen fired on troops restoring order after the capture of a cartel boss on the FBI's most-wanted list. Eight suspects were arrested, showing the violent backlash such arrests can trigger.

items.t: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties
items.d: The two leaders pledged to respect each other's sovereignty after a row over the conflict in eastern Congo, a step that could ease regional diplomacy.

items.t: Belgium strike grounds flights
items.d: A national cost-of-living strike cancelled flights, the latest walkout as the prime minister struggles to pass a budget with spending cuts.

items.t: Seattle airport 'outraged' over ICE arrests
items.d: The airport operator condemned immigration agents detaining a Mexican father and daughter, adding to tension between US cities and federal immigration enforcement.

items.t: Nigeria races to find boat disaster survivors
items.d: Rescuers are searching for missing passengers; the government blamed overcrowding, poor maintenance and lack of life jackets.

items.t: Wall Street rebounds after AI correction
items.d: US stocks rallied strongly as battered chip and AI shares recovered, following a week in which the Nasdaq fell about 10%.

items.t: Capita shares plunge 70% as boss quits
items.d: The outsourcer's chief executive resigned after failures in the civil service pension scheme it runs left public workers facing payment delays.

items.t: HK pushes renminbi as global currency
items.d: Financial secretary Christopher Hui said the yuan is primed to become more attractive internationally, with Hong Kong aiming to be its main offshore hub.

items.t: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $43.9bn deal
items.d: The all-stock takeover would combine two of the biggest cybersecurity firms, creating a giant spanning device and cloud network security.

items.t: US states sue SpaceX, X and xAI over Grok deepfakes
items.d: Virginia and Oregon's attorneys general allege Grok's 'spicy mode' was used to create sexual deepfakes, raising pressure on AI image tools.

items.t: Microsoft prepares for possible loss of OpenAI tech
items.d: Microsoft has teams ready in case OpenAI withdraws licensed technology, and is building its own MAI models as backup.

items.t: Startup raises $277m to run AI on non-Nvidia chips
items.d: Seattle start-up Marlowe, led by ex-Convoy and Microsoft figures, raised a huge seed round at a $1.15bn valuation to rethink AI inference hardware.

items.t: Apple begins rolling out AI Siri across its apps
items.d: The new Siri arrives in eight Apple apps, with a developer preview letting third-party apps plug in.

items.t: Pancreatic cancer drug shrinks tumours in trial
items.d: A new drug shrank tumours and in a few patients made them vanish, offering hope for one of the deadliest cancers; longer trials are needed.

items.t: NHS starts world's largest AI breast screening trial
items.d: Researchers will test whether AI can spot breast cancer earlier and ease pressure on radiologists.

items.t: Snow risk as mild and arctic air clash over UK
items.d: Milder Atlantic air meeting cold arctic air could bring snow to parts of the UK this week.

items.t: PIP assessments need 'fundamental overhaul'
items.d: Disability Minister Sir Stephen Timms will recommend major reforms to how personal independence payment claims are judged.

items.t: Ballymena riot ringleaders jailed
items.d: A mother and son who led riots in County Antrim were jailed, with the judge calling their actions disgraceful.

items.t: Don Toliver postpones O2 show after Manchester scare
items.d: The rapper's London gig was put off after his Manchester concert was evacuated when an unknown substance was released.

items.t: Nvidia黃仁勳復任行政總裁　科技股急升
items.d: Nvidia董事會在罷免黃仁勳不足兩星期後，以美國政府保證為由即時恢復其行政總裁職務。股價急升逾三成，帶動上周AI股拋售後的大反彈。

items.t: 澤連斯基：烏克蘭無人機擊中利比亞港口俄艦
items.d: 澤連斯基表示烏軍襲擊停泊利比亞港口的俄羅斯軍艦，遠離前線。克里姆林宮警告地區局勢升溫，但未直接證實。

items.t: 墨西哥毒梟落網後軍人遇襲
items.d: 槍手向協助恢復秩序的軍人開火，事發前美國聯邦調查局十大通緝要犯之一的毒梟被捕，當局拘捕八名疑犯。

items.t: 肯尼亞與剛果民主共和國同意恢復關係
items.d: 兩國領袖承諾尊重彼此主權，為剛果東部衝突引發的緊張關係降溫。

items.t: 比利時罷工　航班取消
items.d: 全國反生活成本罷工令航班取消，總理至今難以通過削減開支的預算案。

items.t: 西雅圖機場不滿移民局拘捕乘客
items.d: 機場營運機構譴責移民及海關執法局拘捕一對墨西哥籍父女，反映美國城市與聯邦移民執法的矛盾。

items.t: 尼日利亞翻船　搜救爭分奪秒
items.d: 救援人員搜尋失蹤乘客，政府指超載、保養欠佳及缺乏救生衣是主因。

items.t: 華爾街從AI調整中反彈
items.d: 晶片及AI股大幅回升，美股強勁上揚；上周納斯達克指數累跌約一成。

items.t: Capita股價急瀉七成　行政總裁辭職
items.d: 外判商Capita管理的公務員退休金計劃出錯，導致公務員延遲收款，行政總裁請辭。

items.t: 香港推動人民幣國際化
items.d: 財經事務及庫務局局長許正宇表示，人民幣已具備成為國際貨幣的條件，香港將爭取成為主要離岸中心。

items.t: CrowdStrike擬以439億美元收購Zscaler
items.d: 全換股交易將合併兩大網絡保安公司，覆蓋裝置及雲端網絡保安。

items.t: 美國兩州起訴SpaceX、X及xAI　涉Grok深偽圖像
items.d: 維珍尼亞州及俄勒岡州總檢察長指Grok「辛辣模式」被用作製作色情深偽圖像，AI圖像工具面對更大壓力。

items.t: Microsoft準備應對失去OpenAI技術
items.d: Microsoft已組織團隊應對OpenAI收回授權技術的可能，並加緊研發自家MAI模型作後備。

items.t: 初創集資2.77億美元　以非Nvidia晶片運行AI
items.d: 西雅圖初創Marlowe種子輪估值達11.5億美元，旨在重塑AI推理硬件。

items.t: Apple開始在旗下應用推出AI版Siri
items.d: 新Siri登陸八個Apple應用程式，並開放開發者預覽讓第三方應用接入。

items.t: 胰臟癌新藥試驗見效　部分腫瘤消失
items.d: 新藥可縮小腫瘤，少數病人腫瘤更完全消失，為最致命癌症之一帶來希望，但仍需更長期試驗。

items.t: 英國醫療服務展開全球最大AI乳癌篩查試驗
items.d: 研究人員將測試AI能否更早發現乳癌，並減輕放射科醫生壓力。

items.t: 溫和氣流與北極冷空氣交匯　英國或下雪
items.d: 大西洋溫和空氣與北極冷空氣在英國上空交匯，本周部分地區或會下雪。

items.t: 個人獨立生活津貼評估須「根本改革」
items.d: 殘疾事務大臣Stephen Timms將建議大幅改革個人獨立生活津貼的申請評估。

items.t: 巴利米納騷亂主謀判監
items.d: 在安特里姆郡帶頭騷亂的一對母子被判入獄，法官斥其行為可恥。

items.t: 曼徹斯特疏散事件後　Don Toliver押後倫敦演出
items.d: 其曼徹斯特演唱會因有人釋放不明物質而疏散，倫敦O2演出因而押後。
